app.Response.description: The Response struct is used for wrapping the API response with a code, message, and data.

code.description:
Code is the HTTP status code or a custom code used to indicate the result of the request
@example 200

data.description:
Data is the response data (can be any object or null)
@example {"id": 1, "name": "John Doe"}

msg.description:
Msg is the message that describes the result of the request
@example "Request successful"

info.description: Crawlora is a hosted web-data and SERP API: call documented REST endpoints and get normalized JSON instead of HTML to parse — across search/SERP, maps and local, e-commerce, app stores, social, media and finance. One API key; Crawlora runs the proxy rotation, headless browsers and parsing behind the scenes. Billed pay-on-success: charged only on a successful 2xx response, 1-10 credits per call, with a free tier of 2,000 credits per month and no card. A hosted MCP server (mcp.crawlora.net/mcp) exposes the same catalog as agent tools. Search endpoints accept `q` as a universal alias for whichever search-term parameter they document (`query`, `term`, `keyword`, or Amazon's `k`), so one parameter name works across the whole catalog; an explicitly supplied documented name always wins.
info.title: Crawlora API

get.description: Returns an IMDb title chart, chosen with `chart`: `top_rated_movies` (default), `top_rated_tv_shows`, `most_popular_movies`, `most_popular_tv_shows`, `top_rated_english_movies` or `lowest_rated_movies`. `limit` sets the rows (default 25, max 250). Each title has its rank, id, year, rating, rating count and credits.

Lists every value the `type` parameter of the IMDb image endpoints accepts: `behind_the_scenes`, `event`, `poster`, `product`, `production_art`, `publicity`, `still_frame`, `unknown`. Each row carries a display label and a short description.

Returns an IMDb person's profile. Pass exactly one of `id` (such as `nm0634240`) or `url`. The response has the name, biography, birth and death dates, birth place, professions, image and a known-for list of titles with year and credit category.

Returns the awards IMDb lists for a person. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. Each row has the event, year, category, `win` or `nomination` result, award name, recipients and related titles. `total` is the count IMDb lists, and `has_more` is true when fewer rows are returned.

Returns a person's IMDb filmography, grouped into sections such as Actor, Director and Self. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. Each credit has its title, year, role and episode count. A section returns up to 100 credits, so `total` can exceed the rows returned.

Returns image metadata from a person's media index, including the original image URL, dimensions, caption and credited people. Filter by image type with `type`, which accepts a single value or a comma-separated list of: `behind_the_scenes`, `event`, `poster`, `product`, `production_art`, `publicity`, `still_frame`, `unknown`. Omit `type` to return every type. Limit defaults to 50 and clamps to 1000. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`.

parameters.description: Image type filter, single value or comma-separated list
parameters.name: type

get.description: Returns public person video metadata and thumbnail URLs only; playback URLs and media manifests are never returned. IMDb caps the upstream slice at 100 and provides no usable continuation cursor, so `total` can exceed returned rows and `has_more` reports that condition. Limit defaults to 50 and clamps to 100. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`.

Searches IMDb titles by `query`, returning up to `limit` rows (default 10, max 20). Each result has the title id, title, URL, year, title type, image and a description holding the lead cast. A query with no matches returns an empty `results` list.

Returns IMDb advanced title-search results (imdb.com/search/title/). At least one filter is required; sort/limit alone are not enough. Limit defaults to 25 and clamps to 50; only IMDb's first page of results is returned (see `total`/`has_more`), there is no deeper cursor pagination. Genre/company/certificate/country/language/keyword/characters/role are include-only lists; there is no exclude support. Unsupported: genre exclude, three curated `groups` values (best-picture-nominee, best-director-nominee, national-film-registry), and the non-plot "page topic" search fields.

get.description: Returns an IMDb title's details. Pass exactly one of `id` (such as `tt1375666`) or `url`. The response has the title, type, year, release date, runtime, genres, plot, content rating, rating and count, popularity rank, directors and up to three lead cast. Rating and cast fields appear only when present.

Returns the awards IMDb lists for a title. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. Each row has the event, year, category, `win` or `nomination` result, award name, recipients and notes. `total` is the number IMDb lists and `has_more` is true when only part is returned.

Returns a title's public box-office summary: lifetime gross by market (domestic, international, worldwide), the domestic opening weekend, and the production budget. IMDb reports each figure independently, so a real title with no box office data (most TV series, many non-theatrical titles) returns `has_box_office: false` with every figure omitted rather than an error. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`.

Returns the company credits IMDb lists for a title, in sections such as production companies and distributors. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. Each company has its name, URL and a qualifier note. `total` is the count IMDb lists, so a short list is normal on popular titles.

Returns a bounded slice of a title's public connections: other titles it references or is referenced by, such as remakes, spin-offs, "featured in" clips, and "edited into" compilations. `category` is upstream-supplied free text, not a closed enum. IMDb's connections list can run to hundreds or thousands of rows, so `total` can exceed the returned rows and `has_more` reports that condition. Limit defaults to 50 and clamps to 250. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`.

Returns the full cast and crew IMDb lists for a title, in named sections. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. Each credit has a name, IMDb name URL, role and, for cast, the character. The cast returns up to 2,000 rows and other sections up to 100.
Returns public IMDb episode rows for a series title. Limit defaults to 10 and clamps to 20. Optional `season` filters the episodes returned. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`.

Returns the filming locations IMDb lists for a title. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. Each location has its text and an optional note. `total` is the count IMDb lists, `has_more` shows when the list is cut short, and a title with none returns an empty list with `total` 0.

Returns the goofs IMDb lists for a title. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. Each entry in `facts` has the text, a `spoiler` flag and, when IMDb groups it, a category such as Continuity. `total` is the count IMDb lists and `has_more` is true when only part is returned.

Returns image metadata from a title's media index, including the original image URL, dimensions, caption and credited people. Filter by image type with `type`, which accepts a single value or a comma-separated list of: `behind_the_scenes`, `event`, `poster`, `product`, `production_art`, `publicity`, `still_frame`, `unknown`. Omit `type` to return every type. Limit defaults to 50 and clamps to 1000. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`.

parameters.description: Image type filter, single value or comma-separated list
parameters.name: type

get.description: Returns the plot keywords IMDb lists for a title. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. Each keyword has its text and an IMDb search URL for that keyword. `total` is the count IMDb lists, so a short list is normal on popular titles.

Returns the IMDb parental guide for a title. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. Categories such as violence, profanity and frightening scenes carry a severity of `none`, `mild`, `moderate` or `severe` and the guide text. A `summary` gives counts and the highest severity. Spoiler items are excluded.

Returns derived public-page summary metrics for IMDb trivia, goofs, quotes, keywords, filming locations, and company credits. This endpoint is not viewing advice. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. The six sections are gathered from six independent sources, so a section that cannot be fetched is omitted and named in `missing_sections` with `partial` set to `true`, rather than failing the whole response; an error is returned only when no section could be fetched. Callers that require a complete analysis should check `partial`.

Returns the quotes IMDb lists for a title. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. Each entry in `facts` is a whole exchange, with lines prefixed by the speaker, plus a `spoiler` flag. `total` is the count IMDb lists, so a short list is normal on popular titles.
Returns IMDb's aggregate rating, vote count, ten rating buckets, and country rating summaries. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`.

Returns the release dates and alternate titles IMDb lists for a title. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. Releases have a country, date and note; alternate titles have a country, title and type. Both lists are often shorter than `total` and `alternate_titles_total`.
Returns public IMDb user review rows. Limit defaults to 10 and clamps to 20. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`.

Returns the titles in IMDb's More like this recommendations for a title. Pass exactly one of `id` (such as `tt0111161`) or `url`. Each title has its id, name, URL, year, type, runtime, content rating, rating, rating count and image.
Returns public IMDb technical specifications such as runtime, sound mix, color, and aspect ratio. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`.

Returns the trivia IMDb lists for a title. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`. Each entry in `facts` has the text, a `spoiler` flag and, for grouped items, a category such as Director Trademark. `total` is the count IMDb lists and `has_more` is true when only part is returned.

Returns public title video metadata and thumbnail URLs only; playback URLs and media manifests are never returned. IMDb server-truncates this connection and exposes no usable continuation cursor, so `total` can exceed returned rows and `has_more` reports that condition. Limit defaults to 50 and clamps to 100. Pass exactly one of `id` or `url`.
